rows.speaker: بنو تميم
rows.claim: Tamim leaves ما syntactically inactive; Sībawayh calls this the analogical treatment because ما is not a verb and has no implicit subject.
rows.anchor: وأما بنو تميم ~~فيجرونها مجرى أما وهل أي لا يعملونها في شئ

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز
rows.claim: The Hijaz dialect makes ما govern like ليس because the two particles share the meaning of negation.
rows.anchor: وأما أهل الحجاز فيشبهونها بليس إذ كان معناها ~~كمعناها كما شبهوا بها لات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لات only occurs with حين, with an implicit nominative and حين as its accusative object; unlike ليس, it cannot form ordinary subject predicates.
rows.anchor: لا تكون لات ~~إلا مع الحين تضمر فيها مرفوعا وتنصب الحين لأنه مفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لات is restricted to implicit constructions and cannot be inflected or used like ليس with an overt subject or plural subjects.
rows.anchor: لأنها ليست كليس في المخاطبة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports a rare reading of ولات حين مناص, treating لات like ليس in the nominative construction.
rows.anchor: بعضهم قرأ ^ ( و لات حين مناص ) ^ وهي قليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites Saʿd ibn Mālik al-Qaysī’s لا براح as another rare example modeled on ليس and comparable to لات.
rows.anchor: قول سعد بن ~~مالك القيسى # % من فر عن نيرانها % % فأنا ابن قيس لا براح %

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even with حين, لات has limited distribution; Sībawayh compares it with لدن plus غدوة and tāʾ of oath, which are likewise restricted.
rows.anchor: ولا يجاوز بها هذا الحين رفعت أو نصبت ~~ولا تمكن في الكلام كتمكن ليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic phrase ما هذا بشرا exemplifies the Hijaz use of ما like ليس, with بشرا in the accusative.
rows.anchor: @QB@ ما هذا بشرا @QE@ ~~في لغة أهل الحجاز

rows.speaker: بنو تميم
rows.claim: Tamim generally puts the predicate in the nominative in this construction, except for readers who follow the form in the codex.
rows.anchor: وبنو تميم يرفعونها إلا من درى كيف هي في المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the predicate precedes its subject, ما requires the nominative; it cannot behave fully like a verb, and its order is less flexible than verbal constructions.
rows.anchor: فإذا قلت ما منطلق عبد الله أو ما مسئ من أعتب رفعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما زيد إلا منطلق works alike in both dialects; the Qur’anic ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا shows that ما weakens when negation is narrowed by exception.
rows.anchor: @QB@ ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ~~@QE@

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما does not govern strongly when it reverses the sense of ليس, just as it weakens when the predicate is fronted.
rows.anchor: لم تقو ما حيث نقضت معنى ليس كما لم تقو حين قدمت الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ما كان, ما negates كان; in ليس زيد إلا ذاهبا, ما would instead add an affirmative force to the negation.
rows.anchor: أدخلت ما يوجب كما أدخلت ما ينفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With ما, the second negative predicate may be raised as a fresh clause or accusative when coordinated with the first predicate; ليس permits the same alternatives.
rows.anchor: على أن ~~لا تشرك الاسم الآخر في ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is also possible when the second item shares the first particle, as in ليس زيد ذاهبا ولا أخوك منطلقا and ما زيد ذاهبا ولا معن خارجا.
rows.anchor: جعلتها لا التي يكون فيها الاشتراك فتنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh rejects the claim that ما allows only nominative coordination: a second item can share the first ما even when the particle is not repeated.
rows.anchor: في ما إلا الرفع بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fresh clause after ما negates a separate state at the time of speaking; after كان, the negation can cover past and present, while ليس can also refer back to the first item.
rows.anchor: غير كائن في حال حديثك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second predicate can be accusative when it relates to the first subject through a possessive pronoun, as in ما زيد كريما ولا عاقلا أبوه.
rows.anchor: وتقول ما زيد كريما ولا عاقلا أبوه تجعله كأنه للأول بمنزلة كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unrelated predicate such as عاقل عمرو is raised because it does not relate to Zayd; the fronted predicate blocks accusative ما-governance.
rows.anchor: وتقول ما زيد ذاهبا ولا عاقل عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a fronted predicate, a fresh predicate such as ولا كريم أخوه is raised; unlike ما, ليس and كان can license accusative in that position.
rows.anchor: أخوه إن ابتدأته ولم تجعله على ما كما فعلت ذلك حين بدأت بالاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a repeated subject after a fronted predicate, nominative is preferable; accusative is possible but weak because the repeated noun should normally be an implicit pronoun.
rows.anchor: وتقول ما زيد ذاهبا ولا محسن زيد الرفع أجود وإن كنت تريد ~~الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suwād ibn ʿAdī’s verse shows that explicit repetition can nevertheless occur after a negated predicate.
rows.anchor: سواد بن عدى # % لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A repeated explicit name is not equivalent to an attached pronoun; an unrelated overt phrase such as أبو زيد lacks the required connection and is disallowed.
rows.anchor: لأنك قد استغنيت عن إظهاره وإنما ينبغي لك أن ~~تضمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ما أبو زينب ذاهبا ولا مقيمة أمها, the second predicate is raised because the mother is not related to the first subject.
rows.anchor: مقيمة أمها ترفع لأنك لو قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Aʿwar al-Shannī’s verse, مأمورها is attached to the broader referent الأمور, not to the masculine المنهيها; some instead link it to the latter and use genitive.
rows.anchor: فليس بآتيك منهيها % % ولا قاصر عنك مأمورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some poets link مأمورها to منهيها, construing the latter through الأمور; Sībawayh compares Jarīr’s feminine agreement with a partitive antecedent.
rows.anchor: فجعلوا ~~المأمور للمنهى والمنهى هو الأمور لأنه من الأمور وهو بعضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī’s clause coordinates the verbal noun أن تعقرا with أن نردها, even though the injury is not itself the act of returning.
rows.anchor: ليس بمعروف لنا ردها صحاحا ولا مستنكر عقرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh allows the second phrase to be attached to the first by sense; al-Jaʿdī and Dhū al-Rummah support feminine agreement through the horses or winds understood as its referent.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز أن ~~يجر ويحمله على الرد ويؤنث لأنه من الخيل

words: بلى من أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن فله أجره عند ربه ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse first uses singular agreement with من by grammatical form, then plural agreement by meaning in ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون.
rows.anchor: ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accusative alternatives are possible for the coordinated predicates قاصرا and مستنكرا, paralleling other constructions after ليس or ما.
rows.anchor: ولا مستنكرا أن تعقرا ولا قاصرا عنك مأمورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ما كل سوادء تمرة, the second كل may be omitted; بيضاء is then genitive, though شحمة can also be accusative.
rows.anchor: وتقول ما كل سوادء تمرة ولا بيضاء شحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Dāwūd’s verse supports omitting the repeated كل; similarly, split coordination permits genitive or accusative after ما مثل عبد الله.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر أبو دواد # % أكل أمرئ تحسبين امرأ % ونار توقد بالليل نارا % %

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same two case choices apply when the coordinated phrase is separated from its predicate, as in ما مثل عبد الله يقول ذاك ولا أخيه يكره ذاك.
rows.anchor: ما مثل أخيك ولا أبيك يقولان ذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an earlier verb governs the construction, a following coordinated noun may be accusative by the verb’s underlying object relation, even if the first phrase is prepositional.
rows.anchor: لأنه فعل والمجرور فى موضع مفعول منصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jarīr’s بمثل بني بدر and al-Aʿajjāj’s وغورا غائرا illustrate accusative coordination after prepositional phrases through the underlying meanings come and traverse.
rows.anchor: قال جرير # % جئنى بمثل بنى بدر لقومهم % أو مثل أسرة منظور بن سيار %

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verb that only takes a prepositional complement cannot be omitted, since the preposition itself cannot be elided.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تضمر فعلا لا يصل إلا بحرف جر

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s accusative reading وحورا عينا as an instance of the same construction.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا ^ ( وحورا عينا ) ^ فى قراء أبى بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أما and إذا restart the clause, so a later item does not coordinate with an earlier one as it can after ثم or فاء.
rows.anchor: أما وإذا يقطع بهما الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وأما ثمود فهديناهم, nominative after أما follows the particle’s restart of the clause, even where the preceding construction is accusative.
rows.anchor: وقبله نصب وذلك لأنها تصرف الكلام إلى الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن is not a verb: it has no implicit subject and does not allow the same word order as a verb, although it resembles one in its work.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة ضاربين عبد الله وليس بفعل ولا فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in exclamatory ما أحسن عبد الله governs like a verb but lacks verbal inflection, subject behavior, and word-order flexibility; لدن and كم likewise govern without being verbs.
rows.anchor: وليس كالفعل ولم يجئ على أمثلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى behaves like واو, فاء, and ثم for accusative coordination, but unlike أما it depends on the preceding clause and cannot begin one.
rows.anchor: إنما تكون على الكلام الذى قبلها ولا تبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After حتى, accusative is preferred when the following phrase continues the preceding verb, whether the first object is nominative, accusative, or genitive.
rows.anchor: ومما يختار فيه النصب لنصب الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى may mark a limit and govern genitive while the noun remains an underlying object, as in هذا ضارب القوم حتى زيدا يضربه.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت غاية والمجرور مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After هلك القوم حتى زيدا أهلكته, accusative is preferred because the item continues the verb-based construction even when the preceding phrase is genitive.
rows.anchor: هلك القوم حتى زيدا أهلكته أختير النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Case follows semantic object status rather than only surface case: a prepositional object can be accusative in meaning, while a topical subject may still license accusative continuation by its predicate relation.
rows.anchor: إذا قلت عبد الله ضربته إذا كان بعده

words: قل كفى بالله شهيدا بينى وبينكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم, الباء is syntactically present while the underlying construction treats الله as the accusative complement of كفى.
rows.anchor: إنما هى كفى الله ولكنك لما أدخلت الباء عملت

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl analyzes the noun after the preposition as accusative in position and meaning, despite the overt preposition.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الخليل رحمه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noun after حتى may also be raised as a new topic, with its following clause as predicate; this parallels ordinary topical sentences.
rows.anchor: جعلت لقيته مبنيا عليه كما جاز فى الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the phrase after حتى contains no verb, only nominative is available, as in حتى زيد ملقى or حتى زيد مسرح.
rows.anchor: لأنك لم تذكر فعلا فإذا كان فى الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Marwān’s verse ألقى الصحيفة ... حتى نعله ألقاها is cited as poetic evidence for the construction after حتى.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر وهو ابن مروان النحوى # % ألقى الصحيفة كى يخفف رحله % والزاد حتى نعله ألقاها % %
